recipes.name: Aloo Gobi Masala (Cauliflower and Potato Curry)
ingredients_raw: 3 potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch chunks

steps.text: Place the cauliflower in a large, microwave-safe dish; cook in microwave on High for 3 minutes. Transfer the cauliflower to a bowl and set aside. Put the potatoes in the dish and cook in the microwave on High for 4 minutes. Pour into the bowl with the cauliflower.

Heat the olive oil and cumin seeds in a large skillet over medium-high heat until the cumin swells and turns golden brown; stir the onions into the oil and cook about 3 minutes. Add the tomatoes and cook and stir another 3 minutes. Fold the cauliflower and potatoes into the mixture. Season with the curry powder and salt. Continue cooking until completely hot, 3 to 5 minutes. Serve hot.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is great but I never cook in microwave. Steam cauliflower and potatoes, use more curry, blackpeppercorns ground, chop tomatoes and chili poweder or chili flakes. Yummy

I would give this 5 stars for ease and flavor, but I had to make adjustments to the recipe. The seasoning was light, I felt like it needed closer to a tablespoonful of both cumin and curry powder. The pan was also dry, as I used fresh tomatoes, not like the photos at all. Canned, chopped tomatoes would have made the necessary saucy dish, but since I didn't have any, I had to sub by adding tomato paste, water and more seasoning. I will make this again, but add a 10 oz can of chopped tomatoes.

I like this recipe quite a bit. I, like many of the other reviewers, don't microwave cooking much, so, I first roasted the potatoes and cauliflower for 25 min at 475 F instead and it worked out very well. I added peas, too. If you want this dish saucy, I suggest using canned crushed tomatoes instead of fresh. This way,you can adjust sauciness to your liking by varying qty of tomato. I used about 1/2 of a large 28 oz can and it came out great. As others reported, Veg broth would probably work, as well, but, I didn't have any. I also suggest that you double the amount of curry powder that vburrito's published recipe calls for. Bob Appetit!

Wonderful recipe. To make it better add ginger garlic paste and cook the spices first up on slow/medium heat for 10 min. Ensure cauliflower is not cooked a lot so it does not feel very mushy. As potato takes more time to cook, heat them in over for 3-5 min.

I thought this turned out great! I made a few amendments though... Like other reviewers, I prefer not to cook in the microwave if possible. And since I don't have a steamer, I couldn't steam the veggies. Instead, I boiled the cauliflower in chicken stock for 12 minutes, then removed them from the water. Then I boiled the potatoes in the same broth for about 20-25 minutes (until they were soft-ish). Then cooked it all together. I like it spicy, so I added 1 teaspoon of garam masala and 1/2 teaspoon of cayenne pepper. It turned out so delicious! Thank you!

We ate half of it the first night and it was alright. The next day I altered it slightly. I added half a can of full fat coconut milk and simmered that with more tomatoes and added spices such as more cumin, coriander and garam masala. I served it over basmati rice and a piece of chili lime naan. It was like a whole new dish!

This recipe is very good. I agree with other reviewers - steam cauliflower, boil potatoes to firm cooked conditions, and the combine all in one large pan. I also added a pack of sweet peas, steamed, and chopped cilantro in the end. Garnish with cilantro leaves. Do not overcook or it will be mushy. Except onions you cooked in the beginning, all ingredients should have their own texture. I made it many times received great feedback every time

OK, seriously amazing. I love this dish anyway, but the idea of microwaving the potatoes and cauliflower to cut cooking time...brilliant. I sorta merged two versions of this recipe...an old cookbook which had a bunch of spices and traditional cooking methods and this recipe which had modern versions and methods in it. Kept the tomatoes (awesome), used the microwave for the potatoes and cauliflower (brilliant), eliminated the oil (cooking spray), used real ginger and garlic (tsp each), no curry powder as I hate it (sub garam masala for pure awesomeness). Amazingly, this does not include turmeric or cumin (~1/2 tsp each), which I consider crucial (very earthy) but in a pinch the recipe is sufficient as is. I have tried paneer, carrots, chicken, and sweet potatoes for this recipe (dependent on what I have on-hand), all amazing in their own right. If you like a creamier gravy add equal parts milk or cream + broth to the sauce at the end. simmer until thickened. Serves well with chopped cilantro, mango chutney and/or yogurt.

I didn't have cumin seeds so I used a heaping 1/4 tsp of ground cumin. And as others stated, I added 1/3 cup of stock (could use either vegetable or chicken) because I predicted it might be too dry without. It was the perfect moistness!

absolutely delicious! It tastes like a curry dish I picked up in an outdoor market in London. I followed other suggestions adding peas and baking the cauliflower and starch instead of microwaving. Also, I use whatever starch or tubber I have on hand, be it potatoes, rutabaga or turnips. I serve it with Greek yogurt like I ate it in the market and it is perfection. Yum!

As posted this really lacked flavor and sauce. I microwaved the potatoes and cauliflower and thought it was a great time saver. I spiced it as written and even though I had two huge tomatoes it didn’t make a dent in the sauce department. I had to add a cup of chicken broth and I added 1 another tsp of cumin and curry powder, seasoned salt, turmeric and ground garlic.
tasted great but would have liked some sauce
I think you should have weights for the cauliflower, tomatoes, and potatoes. I think it was bland - I needed to add lots more to make it palatable
Subbed sweet potato for potato, added asparagus to steam at the end. Delicious!
Have made this many times. Usually steam the cauliflower and potatoes instead of microwaving. More spices !
It wasnt bad, but definitely bland even after doubling the seasoning.
Very good, family loved it. Wanted to create a sauce for it so added vegetable broth.

I have no idea what I did but I made it and no matter how much I tweaked it was very very bland. the vegetables were still crunchy and my potatoes still tasted raw this is definitely something I will not make again in future
love it
Had to cover and let the potatoes and cauliflower steam another 10 minutes more before they were soft enough to serve.
